Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

45-year-old woman with T2DM presents with 3–4 months of painful, fissured palmar dermatitis beginning after commencing a new housekeeping job with heavy chemical exposure and inconsistent glove use. No systemic symptoms.

Most likely diagnosis: Irritant contact dermatitis of the hands.

Differential diagnoses:  
• Allergic contact dermatitis to cleaning products (moderate likelihood).  
• Chronic hand (atopic) eczema (low likelihood).

Management priorities: reduce irritant exposure, treat inflammation/dryness, monitor response, and ensure follow-up.

Management Plan

- Prescribed topical corticosteroid cream (potency/strength not documented).  
- Prescribed high-emollient moisturizer; advised liberal application 3–4 times daily.  
- Advised strict glove use with all cleaning tasks; avoid known irritant chemicals where possible.  
- Education: expected improvement within 10–14 days; return sooner if spreading or worsening.  
- Follow-up appointment arranged in 1–2 weeks.

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.  
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Irritant contact dermatitis – High likelihood: Temporal link to new job, unprotected chemical exposure, palmar location, pain > itch.  
2. Allergic contact dermatitis – Moderate likelihood: Possible sensitization to cleaning agents; occupational risk; intermittent itch.  
3. Chronic hand eczema – Low likelihood: Chronic xerosis/fissures but no atopic history; occupational trigger more compelling.
